title: Introduce throughput-envelope guard and tenant utilization exporter
author: Maya Patel
description:
Context: We observed intermittent SLA slips during slow scale-down windows where tenants experienced transient throughput drops shortly after nodes were removed. Root-cause analysis showed two contributing factors: (1) the autoscaler was evicting warm state too aggressively for pools with high short-term burst variance, and (2) there was no compact representation of the recent per-tenant throughput envelope available to routing and the admission controller.

What this PR does: Adds a throughput-envelope guard that maintains a compact, decaying quantile snapshot per-tenant (and per-pool) to inform decommit decisions and admission-fallback policies. It also introduces a tenant-utilization-exporter CLI and HTTP endpoint that emits aligned, timestamped utilization timelines (sequential snapshots) for downstream analysis and on-call debugging. The two features together improve safety of scale-downs and make post-incident analysis faster.

Design highlights: - Throughput envelope: a memory-efficient bounded sketch (HDR-like) per tenant that records token/sec percentiles over multiple windows (1m, 5m, 30m) with exponential decay. The envelope exposes: p50/p90/p99, burst index (p99/p50), and a stability score (variance-normalized). - Decommit guard: autoscaler consults the envelope before removing slots from a pool; if a tenant's envelope shows a high burst index or recent p99 spikes, the policy requires an elevated safety margin (elasticity_safety_margin) for that tenant's allocations. - Admission fallback: router uses the envelope to decide whether to route to a full-capacity variant or a cheaper quantized model when the observed workload risk is low. - Tenant util exporter: a unified mechanism to stream snapshots and to export historical timeline fragments in ndjson for forensic tooling and evicition-policy tuning. Includes a small CLI (redwood-util-export) to query S3/DB backfills and produce compact timelines.

Backward compatibility: Default behavior is no-op for clusters that do not enable the guard via config flag (autoscaler.enable_throughput_envelope_guard=false). The exporter is opt-in (telemetry.exporter.enabled=false by default). No schema changes to existing autoscaler DB tables; envelope stores are appended as a new minor table with a TTL.

Testing and validation: - Unit tests for sketch correctness and decay behavior (edge cases around sparsity). - Integration tests with the autoscaler simulator added: simulated burst injection tests where previous policy produced >4x post-scale SLA slips; new policy brings median post-scale latency fold change down to 1.1x in simulations. - End-to-end dogfooding on a small dedicated fleet: 72h soak with synthetic burst patterns and tenant mix; no SLA regressions observed and reduced emergency rollbacks.

Rollout plan: 1) Feature gated behind flags and 24h metric retention toggle. 2) Canary rollout to staging fleets, monitor p99 latency and burst_drop_rate for 48h. 3) Gradual ramp to 20% production pool capacity, with automatic rollback if post-scale p99 increases >8%. 4) Full deployment to dedicated fleets after 7-day bake and SRE sign-off.

Migration notes: The envelope table is populated lazily; historical data is not backfilled. The exporter can be used to reconstruct utilization timelines for important tenants by replaying recent request logs if needed.

Related: ENG-2147 (autoscaler safety margins), ENG-2210 (telemetry export requirements).

feat(autoscaler): consult throughput envelope for decommit guard and elasticity_safety_margin

review_comments: Ethan Ross: The envelope_store memory accounting looks OK but can you add a circuit-breaker to avoid OOM if tenants spike to millions? Also add a prometheus gauge for envelope_count.

Maya Patel: Added allocator-based accounting and a hard cap with evict-oldest policy. Exporter now exposes envelope_count gauge (telemetry/envelope_count) and the CLI emits a size estimate for a requested window.
Priya Khanna: Autoscaler integration looks solid. Please add an explicit unit test for the safety margin math when stability_score is NaN (very sparse tenants).
Maya Patel: Added stability_score NaN guard; defaults to conservative margin when insufficient data.

Luca Moretti: Minor nit: add a short example in docs showing CLI usage to pull the last 12h timeline for a tenant. Also please ensure the rollout checklist includes an emergency rollback metric threshold.
Maya Patel: Docs updated with CLI example and explicit rollback thresholds.
release_notes: Added a throughput-envelope guard to protect scale-downs from removing capacity used for short bursts; added tenant-util-exporter for forensic utilization timelines. Feature is gated and opt-in.
notes_for_oncall: If you see a sudden rise in post-scale p99 after rollout, flip autoscaler.enable_throughput_envelope_guard=false and scale pools manually while we investigate. Use redwood-util-export to fetch recent tenant timelines and inspect burst_index and stability_score.
